mainTopic: Adding a leap month because of טומאה and on the thirtieth of אדר: חזקיהו's mistake, the opinions of רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, and the seasons as a reason to add a month
overview: This amud finishes the ברייתא about חזקיהו, who added a leap month because the people were טמא and then prayed for forgiveness. רבי שמעון says such a leap year counts. In his view חזקיהו's mistake was adding a second ניסן during ניסן, or, in another version, leading the people to keep פסח שני. The גמרא first infers that רבי יהודה holds טומאה is only 'pushed aside' for the public. A ברייתא about the ציץ shows him saying it is fully permitted. The גמרא solves this by filling in missing words in the ברייתא: רבי יהודה actually holds that a leap year made for טומאה does not count, and רבי שמעון allows it even לכתחילה. It explains that חזקיהו added the month on the thirtieth of אדר, a day that שמואל says may already count as ניסן. רב אשי explains the פסח שני version through a doubt about whether women count toward the majority. The amud then discusses what happens if a court adds the month on that thirtieth day, where רבא and רב נחמן disagree. It begins a new rule from שמואל about adding a month because of the seasons.

steps.title: The פסוק about חזקיהו's prayer ends
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes quoting the פסוק that tells how the people ate the קרבן פסח 'not as written' and חזקיהו prayed for forgiveness.
steps.simpleTranslation: …yet they ate the פסח not as is written, for חזקיהו prayed for them, saying: May the good Lord pardon on behalf of…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote from the ברייתא. The ברייתא brings a פסוק from דברי הימים showing that חזקיהו prayed for the people because their פסח was not done properly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק is the evidence רבי יהודה brought from the חזקיהו story. The words 'not as written' and חזקיהו's prayer show that something about that פסח needed forgiveness. רבי שמעון next explains what went wrong, and steps 9–10 show that רבי יהודה actually uses the story to prove that such a leap year does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: The קרבן פסח, the Passover offering
Not as is written, meaning not done according to the rules
חזקיהו, king of יהודה
Will pardon, will atone

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אָכְלוּ אֶת הַפֶּסַח בְּלֹא כַכָּתוּב
phrases.english: yet they ate the Pesach offering not as is written
for Chizkiyahu prayed for them, saying:
May the good Lord pardon on behalf of…
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 30:18. The פסוק goes on to say 'everyone who sets his heart to seek God.'

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אָכְלוּ אֶת הַפֶּסַח בְּלֹא כַכָּתוּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's quote of the פסוק from before this section
steps.raayaObject: That חזקיהו's פסח, after he added a month because of טומאה, was flawed and needed forgiveness
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברי הימים ב 30:18 - the people ate the פסח 'not as written' and חזקיהו prayed for them

steps.title: רבי שמעון: the leap year counts, so why did חזקיהו pray?
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון rules that a year made into a leap year because of טומאה is a valid leap year. He then asks why חזקיהו needed to ask for mercy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: If they made it a leap year because of טומאה, it is a leap year. But then why did חזקיהו ask for mercy for himself?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון gives his ruling: a leap year made because of טומאה still counts. Then he asks a question, setting up his own answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If adding a month because of טומאה is valid, then that was not חזקיהו's mistake. So רבי שמעון has to find a different reason for the prayer in the פסוק. This question opens that search.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritual impurity
They made it a leap year (added a month)
It is a leap year; the added month counts
Asked for mercy, prayed for forgiveness

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון is not saying that adding a month because of טומאה is forbidden. He says that if it was done, it counts. He then looks for a different reason why חזקיהו needed to pray.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
If they made the year a leap year because of impurity,
it is a leap year.
But for what reason
did he ask for mercy for himself?
phrases.notes: 'He' is חזקיהו, from the פסוק just quoted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מִפְּנֵי מָה בִּיקֵּשׁ רַחֲמִים עַל עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reads the same חזקיהו story differently from the proof in step 1
steps.sheelahInformationSought: If a leap year made for טומאה is valid, what did חזקיהו do wrong that needed forgiveness?
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A year made into a leap year because of טומאה is a valid leap year

steps.title: Only אדר may be doubled, and he added ניסן during ניסן
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון answers that חזקיהו's mistake was the timing. He added a second ניסן while already in ניסן, but only אדר may be doubled.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because a leap month may only be a second אדר, and he added a second ניסן while it was already ניסן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון answers his own question. חזקיהו's mistake was not the reason he added the month but the way he did it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The added month must be a second אדר, decided before ניסן begins. חזקיהו waited until ניסן had already started and then declared it a second ניסן. That improper method is what he asked forgiveness for.

keyTerms.meaning: We make a leap year, we add a month
The month of אדר, the only month that may be doubled
Making a second ניסן while already in ניסן

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a clear rule about how a leap year must be made: by adding a second אדר, not by doubling ניסן once it has begun.

phrases.english: Because we add a leap month only as Adar,
and he made a second Nisan during Nisan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 2
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חזקיהו sinned by adding a second ניסן during ניסן, when only אדר may be doubled

steps.title: Another version: he led the people to keep פסח שני
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יהודה, quoting רבי שמעון, gives a different reason for the prayer: חזקיהו convinced the people to keep פסח שני instead of the regular פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן יהודה says in the name of רבי שמעון: It was because he persuaded ישראל to observe פסח שני.
steps.whatsHappening: A second version of רבי שמעון's opinion offers a different explanation of חזקיהו's mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version the story has nothing to do with a leap year. חזקיהו's mistake was having the whole nation skip the first פסח and bring פסח שני, the make-up date a month later. That is what he asked forgiveness for.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of
He persuaded, he led them to do
The second פסח, a month later, for those who missed the first

steps.whatToRemember: There are three readings of חזקיהו's story: (1) רבי יהודה's: as steps 9–10 will show, the story proves that a leap year made because of טומאה does not count; (2) רבי שמעון: the leap year counts, but he wrongly doubled ניסן during ניסן; (3) רבי שמעון בן יהודה in רבי שמעון's name: he wrongly had the people keep פסח שני.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Shimon:
Because he persuaded the Jewish people
to observe the second Pesach.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the question of step 2
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חזקיהו's mistake was leading the nation to keep פסח שני instead of the first פסח

steps.title: רבי יהודה seems to hold impurity is only pushed aside for the public
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to רבי יהודה's ruling that we may add a leap month because of טומאה. It infers that he holds טומאה דחויה בציבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: רבי יהודה says we may add a leap month. This shows that רבי יהודה holds that impurity is only pushed aside for the public.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the ברייתא has been quoted, the גמרא starts to analyze it. It draws a conclusion about what רבי יהודה must hold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If טומאה were fully permitted for the community, there would be no reason to add a month just to avoid bringing the פסח in טומאה. Since רבי יהודה wants to delay so the people can be pure, he must hold that טומאה is only 'pushed aside' (דחויה). That means it is allowed when there is no choice, but we should avoid it when we can.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said; a formula that quotes back an earlier source to discuss it
Apparently, this shows
Pushed aside: allowed only when needed, but still to be avoided
The community, the public

steps.confusionAlert: דחויה (pushed aside) and הותרה (fully permitted) are two different positions. דחויה means we try to avoid טומאה if we can, for example by adding a month. הותרה means טומאה is simply not a problem for the community.

phrases.english: The Master said:
Rabbi Yehuda says: We may add a leap month.
Apparently, Rabbi Yehuda holds:
impurity is only pushed aside for the public.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מְעַבְּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי יהודה's ruling in the ברייתא and draws a conclusion from it
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From רבי יהודה's ruling, the גמרא infers that he holds טומאה דחויה בציבור

steps.title: Challenge from the dispute about the ציץ
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי שמעון and רבי יהודה argue about whether the ציץ brings forgiveness only while it is on the כהן גדול's forehead. This opens a challenge to the inference about רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it taught: The ציץ brings acceptance whether it is on his forehead or not; this is רבי שמעון's view. רבי יהודה says: While it is still on his forehead it brings acceptance; if it is no longer on his forehead it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a challenge with 'והא תניא' by quoting a ברייתא about the ציץ. This step sets up the contradiction; the ברייתא continues in the next two steps, where the problem becomes clear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ציץ, the gold plate worn by the כהן גדול, makes a קרבן brought in טומאה acceptable. In this dispute רבי יהודה takes the stricter view that the ציץ works only while worn. The rest of the ברייתא will show that he treats טומאה בציבור as fully permitted (הותרה), which clashes with step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא? A formula that opens a challenge
The gold head-plate worn by the כהן גדול
His forehead
Brings acceptance, makes the קרבן acceptable despite טומאה
While it is still

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a baraita:
The Tzitz, whether it is on his forehead
phrases.notes: 'His forehead' means the כהן גדול's forehead.

phrases.english: or whether it is not on his forehead, brings acceptance;
these are the words of Rabbi Shimon.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
While it is still on his forehead, it brings acceptance;

phrases.aramaic: אֵין עוֹדוֹ עַל מִצְחוֹ – אֵינוֹ מְרַצֶּה.
phrases.english: if it is no longer on his forehead, it does not bring acceptance.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא תַּנְיָא צִיץ בֵּין שֶׁיֶּשְׁנוֹ עַל מִצְחוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference in step 5 about רבי יהודה's view
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יהודה holds טומאה דחויה בציבור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא about the ציץ will go on to show רבי יהודה treating טומאה בציבור as fully permitted (הותרה). That contradicts the inference that he holds it is only pushed aside.

steps.title: רבי שמעון brings proof from the כהן גדול on יום הכיפורים
steps.stepSummary: Inside the ברייתא, רבי שמעון argues that the ציץ brings forgiveness even when it is not on the forehead. His proof is יום הכיפורים, when the כהן גדול serves without the ציץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said to him: The כהן גדול on יום הכיפורים proves it. The ציץ is not on his forehead, and it still brings acceptance.
steps.whatsHappening: We are still inside the ברייתא that opened in the last step. רבי שמעון brings a proof against רבי יהודה's view that the ציץ works only while it is being worn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום הכיפורים the כהן גדול does part of the service in white linen garments, without the ציץ. Yet the service is accepted. So, says רבי שמעון, the ציץ must help even when it is not on his forehead.

keyTerms.meaning: The golden plate worn on the כהן גדול's forehead. It brings forgiveness for certain טומאה problems with קרבנות.
Will prove it. Used to bring a case that disproves the other side.
Brings acceptance or forgiveness for the קרבן.
His forehead.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said to him:
The High Priest on Yom Kippur will prove it,
for it is not on his forehead, and it still brings acceptance.
phrases.notes: "It" is the ציץ. During part of the יום הכיפורים service he wears only white garments, without it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in step 6 with רבי שמעון's proof.
steps.raayaObject: The ציץ brings forgiveness even when it is not on the forehead.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The יום הכיפורים service, done without the ציץ, is still accepted.

steps.title: רבי יהודה says יום הכיפורים is different because טומאה is permitted for the public
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה rejects the proof. On יום הכיפורים all the קרבנות are public ones, and for the public טומאה is simply permitted, so the ציץ is not needed there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said to him: Leave יום הכיפורים aside, because impurity is permitted for the public.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה pushes away רבי שמעון's proof. This line also finishes the challenge against step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה says טומאה הותרה בציבור: for the public, טומאה is fully allowed. But step 5 inferred that he holds טומאה דחויה בציבור, which is why he would add a leap month to avoid טומאה. If טומאה is fully allowed, why bother adding a month? That is the contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: Leave it aside. Your case is different.
For the public, ritual impurity is fully permitted, not just pushed aside.
The public, the community as a whole.

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the two words. דחויה means טומאה is only pushed aside, so we should still try to avoid it. הותרה means it is fully allowed, so there is nothing to avoid. Step 5 said רבי יהודה holds דחויה; here he seems to say הותרה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said to him:
Leave aside Yom Kippur,
because impurity is permitted for the public.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי שמעון's proof inside the ברייתא. In the larger sugya it completes the challenge to step 5's inference.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי שמעון's proof from יום הכיפורים.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: On יום הכיפורים the קרבנות are public, and public טומאה is permitted anyway, so the case shows nothing about the ציץ.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference in step 5 that רבי יהודה holds טומאה דחויה בציבור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי יהודה holds הותרה, there is no reason to add a leap month to avoid טומאה.

steps.title: The earlier ברייתא contradicts itself anyway
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers back that even without this question, the earlier ברייתא is hard to understand. רבי יהודה says we may add a leap month, but then he tells of חזקיהו asking for mercy for doing exactly that.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by your logic, the teaching itself should bother you. רבי יהודה says we add a leap month. Then רבי יהודה tells of חזקיה, king of יהודה, who made the year a leap year because of impurity and asked for mercy for himself.
steps.whatsHappening: Instead of answering directly, the גמרא shows that the earlier ברייתא has its own internal problem. That problem will lead to the real answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יהודה allows a leap year for טומאה, why would his own story show חזקיהו begging forgiveness for doing it? The story fits better with someone who says it should not be done. So our reading of the ברייתא must be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your own reasoning. It turns a problem back on the questioner.
The source itself should be difficult for you.
Asked for mercy. He prayed for forgiveness.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
the teaching itself should be difficult for you:
Rabbi Yehuda says: we make it a leap year,
and Rabbi Yehuda said:
There was an incident with Hezekiah, king of Judah,
who made the year a leap year because of impurity,
and he asked for mercy for himself?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by showing that the source behind step 5 is itself hard to read.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier ברייתא as it reads now: רבי יהודה says מעברין and also tells the חזקיהו story.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה's ruling and his story contradict each other.

steps.title: The ברייתא is missing words: רבי יהודה says the leap year is not valid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the ברייתא. The תנא קמא says we should not add the month for טומאה, but if it was done, it counts. רבי יהודה says it does not count, and he brings חזקיהו as proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, words are missing, and this is what it teaches: We do not make the year a leap year because of impurity, but if they did, it is a leap year. רבי יהודה says: it is not a leap year. And רבי יהודה said, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the ברייתא has words missing and fills them in. Now רבי יהודה is the one against adding a leap month for טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this fix, the חזקיהו story fits רבי יהודה: חזקיהו prayed because his leap year was not valid. It also fits רבי יהודה's view of טומאה הותרה בציבור, because if טומאה is allowed there is no reason to add a month. So the inference in step 5 falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Words are missing, and this is how it should read.
It is a leap year. The added month counts.
To make a year into a leap year by adding a month.

steps.whyThisMatters: This changes the whole picture. Step 5 thought רבי יהודה allows a leap year for טומאה. Now we see he does not, and the rest of the sugya is built on this fixed version.

phrases.english: Rather, words are missing
and this is what it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְעַבְּרִין אֶת הַשָּׁנָה מִפְּנֵי הַטּוּמְאָה,
phrases.english: We do not make the year a leap year because of impurity,
but if they did make it one, it is a leap year.
Rabbi Yehuda says: it is not a leap year.
And Rabbi Yehuda said, etc.
phrases.notes: The "etc." points back to the חזקיהו story. Now it is his proof that such a leap year does not count.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves step 9's contradiction, and with it the problem from steps 5 to 8, by filling in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה allows adding a leap month because of טומאה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה holds that a leap year made because of טומאה is not valid. That fits both the חזקיהו story and טומאה הותרה בציבור.

steps.title: Now רבי שמעון seems to say the same as the תנא קמא
steps.stepSummary: With the new reading, the תנא קמא already says that if it was done, it counts. רבי שמעון says the same thing, so what is he adding?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, רבי שמעון says: If they made it a leap year because of impurity, it is a leap year. Isn't that the same as the תנא קמא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the fix it just made. It now leaves two opinions in the ברייתא saying the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the fixed version, both the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון agree that the leap year counts after the fact. A ברייתא would not list רבי שמעון separately if he did not disagree, so there must be some difference.

keyTerms.meaning: If so. If your explanation is right.
That is the same as the first, unnamed opinion.

phrases.english: If so,
Rabbi Shimon says:
If they made it a leap year because of impurity, it is a leap year.
Isn't that the same as the first Tanna?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the fixed reading from step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The fixed version of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: After the fix, רבי שמעון and the תנא קמא say the same thing, so one of them is not needed.

steps.title: רבא: They argue about doing it from the start
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the difference. The תנא קמא says we should not add the month for טומאה, though it counts if done. רבי שמעון says we may do it even from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The difference between them is about doing it from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge by pointing to a difference between the two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that after the fact (בדיעבד) the leap year counts. They argue about לכתחילה: may a בית דין plan to add the month because of טומאה? The תנא קמא says no; רבי שמעון says yes.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start. What one should do in the first place.
There is a difference between them.
After the fact. Once it has already been done.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The difference between them is about doing it from the start.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pointing to a practical difference (לכתחילה vs. בדיעבד)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון and the תנא קמא say exactly the same thing.
steps.terutzMaskana: They agree about after the fact, but רבי שמעון allows it from the start and the תנא קמא does not.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבא, and it explains חזקיהו's mistake
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says exactly what רבא said: the תנא קמא forbids it לכתחילה and רבי שמעון allows it. It then explains that חזקיהו prayed because he added a second ניסן instead of a second אדר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: We do not make the year a leap year because of impurity from the start. רבי שמעון says: we do. So why did חזקיהו ask for mercy for himself? Because we only add a second אדר, and he added a ניסן during ניסן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רבא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the word לכתחילה, just as רבא said. Since רבי שמעון allows the leap year, he must explain חזקיהו's prayer some other way: the problem was not the טומאה but the timing. Only אדר may be doubled, and חזקיהו added a month when it was already ניסן.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא also teaches this. It brings support.
The month that is doubled in a leap year.
Adding a second ניסן while already in ניסן.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
We do not make the year a leap year
because of impurity from the start.
Rabbi Shimon says: we do make it a leap year.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מִפְּנֵי מָה בִּקֵּשׁ רַחֲמִים עַל עַצְמוֹ?
phrases.english: So why did he ask for mercy for himself?
phrases.notes: "He" is חזקיהו. This is the same answer רבי שמעון gave back in step 3.

phrases.english: Because we only add a second Adar,
and he added a Nisan during Nisan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that supports רבא's answer in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון argue about לכתחילה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that uses the word לכתחילה and has רבי שמעון saying מעברין.

steps.title: How could חזקיהו add a second ניסן? The תורה says only one month is ניסן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא and asks: does חזקיהו not know the teaching from "החדש הזה לכם" that only this month is ניסן, and no other month can be ניסן?
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: Because we only add a second אדר, and he added a ניסן during ניסן. But doesn't חזקיהו hold the teaching of "החדש הזה לכם" ("This month shall be for you"): this is ניסן, and no other month is ניסן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the ברייתא and questions it. A great king like חזקיהו would surely know there is no second ניסן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק teaches that only one month can be ניסן, so adding a second ניסן is plainly wrong. It is hard to believe חזקיהו did not know such a basic rule. So how did he make this mistake?

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said. It quotes a line already taught so it can be discussed.
But doesn't he hold? Does he not accept this?
"This month shall be for you." The פסוק about ניסן being the first month.

phrases.english: The Master said:
Because we only add a second Adar,
and he added a Nisan during Nisan.
But doesn't Hezekiah hold
"This month shall be for you":
this is Nisan, and no other month is Nisan!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: שֶׁאֵין מְעַבְּרִין אֶלָּא אֲדָר, וְהוּא עִיבֵּר נִיסָן בְּנִיסָן. וְלֵית לֵיהּ לְחִזְקִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the end of step 13's ברייתא and asks about it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that חזקיהו added a second ניסן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק clearly rules out a second ניסן, so חזקיהו could not have made such a basic mistake.

steps.title: חזקיהו made שמואל's mistake: he added the month on the thirtieth of אדר
steps.stepSummary: חזקיהו did not knowingly add a second ניסן. He added the month on the thirtieth of אדר. As שמואל teaches, that day may already count as ניסן, so adding then is like adding in ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: He erred in שמואל's rule. שמואל said: We do not make a leap year on the thirtieth day of אדר, since that day is fit to be set as the first of ניסן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that חזקיהו's mistake was a subtle one about timing, the rule that שמואל later taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The thirtieth of אדר could become ראש חודש ניסן, so it already carries ניסן's status. חזקיהו thought it was still אדר and added a month then. In truth that counted as adding ניסן in ניסן.

keyTerms.meaning: He made the mistake that שמואל's rule addresses.
The thirtieth day of אדר, which could become ראש חודש ניסן.
Fit to be set as the start of the new month.

steps.whatToRemember: The final picture: the תנא קמא says not to add a leap month for טומאה, but it counts if done. רבי יהודה says it does not count. רבי שמעון says it may be done even לכתחילה. Under רבי שמעון, חזקיהו's only mistake was adding the month on the thirtieth of אדר, a day that could already be ניסן.

phrases.english: He erred in Shmuel's rule,
for Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְעַבְּרִין אֶת הַשָּׁנָה בְּיוֹם שְׁלֹשִׁים שֶׁל אֲדָר,
phrases.english: We do not make the year a leap year on the thirtieth day of Adar,
since it is fit to be set as Nisan.
phrases.notes: That day might become ראש חודש ניסן, so adding a month then counts as adding in ניסן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14 by explaining how חזקיהו's mistake happened.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: a subtle error about timing
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חזקיהו knowingly added a month during ניסן itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: He added it on the thirtieth of אדר, not knowing that this day already has the status of ניסן.

steps.title: Why חזקיהו thought he could add the month on that day
steps.stepSummary: חזקיהו did not hold of the idea 'since it is fit to be ניסן', so he treated the thirtieth of אדר as plain אדר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he (חזקיהו) held: we do not say 'since it is fit.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer from the last step by explaining what חזקיהו was thinking. He believed the thirtieth of אדר is simply אדר, even though it could have become ניסן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל says that because the thirtieth of אדר could be declared the first of ניסן, we treat it like ניסן. חזקיהו did not accept this 'הואיל וראוי' idea, so he thought adding the month that day was fine. That is why he did not see himself as adding a second ניסן.

keyTerms.meaning: Since it is fit; we treat something as what it could become
We do not say (we do not use this reasoning)
He (here, חזקיהו)

phrases.english: And he held:
phrases.notes: 'He' is חזקיהו, the king from the last step.

phrases.english: We do not say 'since it is fit.'
phrases.notes: Since the day was fit to become ניסן, שמואל treats it as ניסן. חזקיהו did not accept that.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer of step 15 by explaining חזקיהו's reasoning.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the mistake: חזקיהו used a different principle, so he did not knowingly break the rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חזקיהו seems to have openly gone against 'החדש הזה לכם' by making a second ניסן.
steps.terutzMaskana: He held that the thirtieth of אדר is just אדר, so he thought he was adding a second אדר, not a second ניסן.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports שמואל
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says what שמואל said: we do not add the month on the thirtieth of אדר, because that day can become ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also taught in a ברייתא: We do not add a month to the year on the thirtieth of אדר, since it is fit to be set as ניסן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that matches שמואל's rule, the rule חזקיהו did not hold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 used שמואל's teaching to explain חזקיהו. Now a ברייתא shows that this is not only שמואל's own opinion; an older teaching says the same thing. This backs up the claim that חזקיהו was mistaken.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also taught this way in a ברייתא
Adding a month to make the year a leap year
To set it (to declare the day as the new month)

phrases.english: It is also taught so:
We do not add a month to the year
on the thirtieth day of אדר,
since it is fit to be set as ניסן.
phrases.notes: If the court declares the new month that day, the thirtieth becomes the first of ניסן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up שמואל's teaching quoted in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's rule that we do not add the month on the thirtieth of אדר
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the same wording and reason

steps.title: רבי שמעון's other reason for חזקיהו's prayer
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: רבי שמעון בן יהודה, quoting רבי שמעון, says חזקיהו prayed because he led the people to keep פסח שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן יהודה says in the name of רבי שמעון: Because he led the Jewish people to keep פסח שני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא about חזקיהו and quotes another opinion about why he asked for forgiveness. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the mistake is not about the calendar. חזקיהו is blamed for sending the people to פסח שני when they should have brought the פסח at its regular time. The גמרא will now ask how such a mistake could happen.

keyTerms.meaning: Led, caused (someone to do something)
The second פסח, a month later, for those who could not bring the first
In the name of

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: רבי שמעון בן יהודה says in the name of רבי שמעון:
Because he led the Jewish people
to keep the second פסח.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the original ברייתא (step 4) to analyze its second explanation of חזקיהו's prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חזקיהו's mistake was sending the people to פסח שני.

steps.title: What was the situation?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the case was, so that חזקיהו would send the people to פסח שני and later regret it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the details of the story. It is setting up רב אשי's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually it is clear who brings the first פסח and who waits for the second. For a great king to make a mistake here, the case must have been unclear. The גמרא wants to know what made it unclear.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What does it look like?

phrases.english: What is the case?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the details of רבי שמעון's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The case in which חזקיהו could wrongly send the people to פסח שני.

steps.title: רב אשי: half impure, half pure, and the women decide
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains: half the people were impure and half pure, and the women added to the pure side gave it the majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: For example, the Jewish people were half impure and half pure, and the women completed the pure side and made it bigger.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי describes the case. Counting only the men, the impure were the majority. Counting the women too, the pure were the majority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The halacha depends on whether the impure are a majority or a minority of the people. Here the answer changes depending on whether women count. So everything depends on one question: are women obligated in the first פסח?

keyTerms.meaning: Half
Impure people / pure people
Complete, fill up (the number)
Are more than, exceed

phrases.english: רב אשי said:
For example, where the Jewish people were
half impure, half pure,
phrases.notes: He means the men: half of them were impure.

phrases.english: and the women completed the pure
and made them more than the impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: כְּגוֹן שֶׁהָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A case where the majority depends on whether the women are counted.

steps.title: How חזקיהו changed his mind about the women
steps.stepSummary: At first חזקיהו held women must bring the first פסח, so the impure were a minority and were sent to פסח שני. Later he held women only may, so the impure were a majority and should not have been sent.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first he thought: women are obligated in the first פסח, so the impure are a minority, and a minority is pushed off to פסח שני. In the end he thought: women are only allowed in the first פסח, so the impure are the majority, and the majority is not pushed off to פסח שני.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי finishes his explanation by showing חזקיהו's first view and his later view. His later view showed that he had sent the people away by mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only a minority is impure, they wait for פסח שני. If the majority is impure, everyone brings the פסח on time even in טומאה. Once חזקיהו decided women are not obligated, the impure men were the majority, so they should have brought the first פסח. That is why he asked for forgiveness.

keyTerms.meaning: An obligation
Optional; allowed but not required
A minority
The majority
Are pushed off (to a later date)

steps.whatToRemember: A minority who are impure wait for פסח שני, but if the majority are impure they bring the first פסח. חזקיהו's mistake came from first counting the women and then realizing they are not obligated.

phrases.english: At first he thought:
women are obligated in the first,
phrases.notes: 'The first' means the regular פסח on the fourteenth of ניסן.

phrases.english: so the impure are a minority,
and a minority is pushed off to the second פסח.
And in the end he thought:
women are only allowed in the first,
so the impure are the majority,
phrases.notes: Without the women, only the men are counted, and the men were mostly impure.

phrases.english: and a majority is not pushed off to the second פסח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב אשי's answer and explains exactly where חזקיהו went wrong.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חזקיהו changed his mind about whether women are obligated, and that changed who was the majority.

steps.title: Back to שמואל's rule itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to discuss שמואל's teaching on its own: we do not add the month on the thirtieth of אדר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself. שמואל said: We do not add a month to the year on the thirtieth of אדר, since it is fit to be set as ניסן.
steps.whatsHappening: With the word גופא, the גמרא goes back to study שמואל's rule by itself. This sets up the questions about what happens after the fact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now שמואל's rule was used only to explain חזקיהו. Now the גמרא repeats it on purpose so it can ask new questions about it. The rule tells us what to do from the start, but not what happens if a court did it anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself; going back to look at a quoted teaching
An אמורא who taught this rule

phrases.english: The matter itself. שמואל said:
We do not add a month to the year
on the thirtieth day of אדר,
since it is fit to be set as ניסן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the חזקיהו story and returns to study שמואל's rule by itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the start, a court may not add the month on the thirtieth of אדר.

steps.title: What if they did add the month on that day?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if a court did add the month on the thirtieth of אדר, what is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: If they added the month, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about after the fact: the court went ahead and added the month on that day. This sets up עולא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל only said we should not do it. The question is whether adding the month still works, and what the court should do next.

keyTerms.meaning: They made it a leap year (they added the month)
What (is the law)?

phrases.english: If they added the month, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about after the fact on שמואל's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The law when a court added the month on the thirtieth of אדר.

steps.title: עולא: do not declare the new month that day
steps.stepSummary: עולא says the added month stands, and the court should not declare the new month on that day.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: We do not declare the new month.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers that we protect the added month by not making that day into ניסן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The added month works as long as the thirtieth stays אדר. If the court does not declare the new month that day, the day stays אדר, and the month was really added in אדר.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא
Declaring the start of a new month

phrases.english: עולא said:
We do not declare the new month.
phrases.notes: He means on that thirtieth day, so it stays אדר and the added month counts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The added month stands; the court does not declare the new month that day.

steps.title: What if they declared the new month anyway?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the court did declare the new month that day, what is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: If they declared the new month, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes one step further: the court added the month and also declared that day the new month. This sets up a disagreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the two acts clash. Adding the month needs the day to be אדר, but declaring the new month makes it ניסן. Which one wins?

keyTerms.meaning: They declared the new month

phrases.english: If they declared the new month, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the case that עולא said should not happen.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The law when a court both added the month and declared the new month on the thirtieth of אדר.

steps.title: רבא: the added month is cancelled
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that declaring the new month cancels the added month.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The added month is cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers that once the day became ניסן, the month turns out to have been added in ניסן, so it does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Declaring the new month made the thirtieth the first of ניסן. So the month was added in ניסן, which is not allowed, and it is cancelled. This fits the idea that no month can be a second ניסן.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא
The added month is cancelled

phrases.english: רבא said:
The added month is cancelled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Declaring the new month wins, and the added month is cancelled.

steps.title: רב נחמן: both count
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן disagrees: the year has the added month, and the new month is declared too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: It has the added month and the new month is declared.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives a different answer from רבא. Both things the court did stay in place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא says declaring the new month cancels the added month. רב נחמן says each act works on its own, so neither one cancels the other. The year is a leap year, and the new month is declared as well.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא
Has the added month (a leap year)
Declared (the new month stands)

steps.whatToRemember: From the start we do not add the month on the thirtieth of אדר (שמואל). If it was done, עולא says we do not declare the new month that day. If the new month was declared too, רבא says the added month is cancelled, and רב נחמן says both count.

phrases.english: רב נחמן said:
It has the added month and the new month is declared.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבא's answer in step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both acts stand: the year has the added month and the new month is declared.

steps.title: רבא's challenge: a late leap month could make people careless about חמץ
steps.stepSummary: רבא attacks רב נחמן's view that a month added on the thirtieth of אדר still stands even after the new month was declared. By then people have been learning הלכות פסח for thirty days, so pushing פסח off by a month could lead them to treat חמץ lightly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נחמן: From פורים to פסח is thirty days, and from פורים we already teach הלכות פסח. A ברייתא says people ask about הלכות פסח thirty days before פסח, though רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says two weeks. So if the court waits until the new month arrives and then pushes פסח away, people will come to take חמץ lightly!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רב נחמן's ruling from the previous step that a month added on the thirtieth of אדר still counts. He points to a real-life problem this would cause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Thirty days before פסח everyone is already preparing for פסח. If the court suddenly adds a month at the last moment, people may think the dates are random. Then they may not take the חמץ rules seriously when פסח really comes.

keyTerms.meaning: פורים
the laws of פסח
the start of the month, ראש חודש
they push it further away
to treat lightly, to be careless about
leavened food, which is forbidden on פסח

phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Nachman:
Now, from Purim to Pesach
there are thirty days,
and starting from Purim we teach the laws of Pesach,
as it is taught in a baraita:
People ask about the laws of Pesach
starting thirty days before Pesach.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: שְׁתֵּי שַׁבָּתוֹת.
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: two weeks before.
So when the new month arrives,
will they push it away?
phrases.notes: "It" means פסח. Adding a month moves פסח a whole month later.

phrases.english: People will come to treat chametz lightly!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב נַחְמָן מִכְּדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's ruling in step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's view that a month added on the thirtieth of אדר stands even though the new month is declared.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: People have already been preparing for פסח for thirty days. A last-minute delay would make them see the calendar as random and become careless about חמץ.

steps.title: רב נחמן: people know a leap year depends on calculation
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that people know leap years depend on careful calculation. They will assume the calculation was only finished now, so they will not take חמץ lightly.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: People surely know that a leap year depends on calculation. They will say: the calculation simply did not come out for the רבנן until now.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן defends his ruling against רבא's challenge. He says people will not lose respect for the calendar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's fear was that a late change looks random. רב נחמן says people understand the calendar comes from complicated calculations. A late decision just looks like the math took longer, so the dates still feel trustworthy.

keyTerms.meaning: they certainly know
a leap year, with an added month
the calculation
came out, was finished

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן holds that if a court added the month on the thirtieth of אדר and also declared the new month, both acts still count. People understand that the calendar depends on calculation, so they will not become careless about חמץ.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רב נחמן answering רבא.

phrases.english: People surely know
that with a leap year,
the matter depends on calculation.
They will say:
phrases.notes: Here "they" means ordinary people, not the רבנן.

phrases.aramaic: חוּשְׁבָּנָא הוּא דְּלָא סְלֵיק לְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן
phrases.english: It is the calculation that did not come out for the Rabbis
until now.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge from step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the premise that people will see the change as random.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A last-minute leap month would make people doubt the calendar and take חמץ lightly.
steps.terutzMaskana: People know leap years depend on calculation. They will see the late decision as the calculation finishing late, so respect for חמץ stays.

steps.title: שמואל: add a month only if the season would be short by most of a month
steps.stepSummary: A new topic begins. רב יהודה quotes שמואל: the court adds a month to the year only if the season would be lacking most of a month.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: We do not add a month to the year unless the season was lacking most of a month.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: when the seasons of the year require adding a month. שמואל gives the basic rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps discussed when the court may add a month. Now שמואל sets a minimum based on the seasons. A small gap is not enough to add a month; the season must be off by most of a month.

keyTerms.meaning: making the year a leap year by adding a month
a season of the solar year
lacking, short
most of a month

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
We do not add a month to the year
unless the season was
lacking most of a month.
phrases.notes: The season meant is the summer season, and the month is תשרי. Summer would still be running for most of תשרי.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל אֵין מְעַבְּרִין אֶת הַשָּׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about adding a month because of the seasons.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A month is added only if the season would be short by most of a month.

steps.title: How much is "most of a month"?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how many days count as "most of a month" in שמואל's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much is "most of a month"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for an exact number to define שמואל's phrase. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Most of a month" is not exact enough to rule by. The גמרא wants the exact number of days that triggers adding a month.

keyTerms.meaning: and how much

phrases.english: And how much is "most of a month"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a definition of a term in step 30.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact number of days meant by "most of a month".

steps.title: Sixteen days, according to רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The answer: sixteen days. This is the view of רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sixteen days; these are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question: "most of a month" means sixteen days. It names רבי יהודה as the one who holds this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A month has about thirty days, so sixteen days is just over half. Saying "the words of רבי יהודה" tells us this is one view, and other views may follow.

keyTerms.meaning: sixteen days
the words of רבי יהודה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבי יהודה, the תנא named here, with רב יהודה, the אמורא who quoted שמואל in step 30. They are two different people.

phrases.english: Sixteen days;
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: שִׁשָּׁה עָשָׂר יוֹם דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "Most of a month" means sixteen days, according to רבי יהודה.
